example_teams.team_notes: Though Shorekeeper is ideal, Iuno+Verina should be stronger than any Mono Fusion/F2P team alternatives by a slight margin (excluding quickswap).

Use Mortefi on Moonlit Clouds with the Stonewall Bracer main Echo in the 2nd slot, or use Mornye on Halo of Starry Radiance with the Spacetrek Explorer main Echo in the 3rd slot so Lupa can Outro buff Jingran, based on your team.

In these teams, Shorekeeper should run the Halo of Starry Radiance set with the Spacetrek Explorer main Echo. Mortefi or Rebecca with Verina should be on Stonewall Bracer (make sure to use it before Rebecca's rotation if you're using the Rebecca+Verina team).

cons: One of the most Signature weapon-reliant characters in the game. Limited weapon alternatives seem good on paper, but don't compensate for the big increase in power and build accessibility his weapon provides, not to mention how much worse the permanent options are;
Possesses no good purple tokens in Whimpering Wastes, so he will be more difficult to use there once his dedicated gold token is gone;
Very low quickswap potential in his ideal teams, much like a good chunk of the modern DPS cast.
pros: One of the strongest and most accessible DPS releases in a while. Only requires his Signature weapon to perform at a very high level;
Strong sequence value, particularly in his S2 and S6;
Damage is spread out very evenly across his rotation in pretty good AoE - good for multi-wave content;
Has access to a multitude of team options, bringing older characters back into the meta while utilizing new ones to great effect as well, getting a team up and running for him is easy overall;
Found on some social media under the alias XxX_D4rkS4suk3_XxX. He's so dark and edgy like me fr.

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Jingran is a 5-star Fusion Heavy Attack DPS character who relies on the Shield generation mechanic, exactly like Augusta & Iuno, in order to gain great buffs to his damage. The bulk of his damage will be concentrated in several Forte Heavy attacks that he needs to build up throughout his rotation.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics
paragraphs: Jingran has 2 stances, Yin Vessel and Yang Font. He starts in Yang Font stance by default, and switches between them upon casting his Forte Heavy attacks. Each mode has its unique set of attacks, including Basic Attacks, Skills, and Forte Heavies.

Much of Jingran's stat increases are based on his Max HP, which should be built up to 50000 to gain a massive amount of ATK, DMG Bonus, Incoming Healing Bonus, and multiplier increase on the Forte Heavies from a resource called Fire of Life, acquired via his Ultimate. The stat increases are such a huge help that they are valued over CRIT stats for him.

Finally, Jingran can get this extra DMG Bonus based on his HP and the amount of Shields he and his teammates can apply throughout their rotation. Once per rotation, having a teammate apply another Shield grants a lot of stacks of Ghost Shroud, this resource is consumed upon using his Intro and grants him a massive amount of Fusion DMG Bonus. So having Shields applied by teammates is quite important. Jingran also applies small Shields to himself every time he deals damage up to once every 0.5s, and has 0 DEF to compensate for his desire to build a very high HP stat and the Incoming Healing increases that result from it.

sections.heading: Rotation Mechanics & Explanation
paragraphs: Jingran builds up his Forte resource, called Qi, by casting Basic Attack stage 3&4 (50), Dodge Counters, Skills, Intros (100), Ultimates and Forte Heavies (200). The resource stacks up to 300, at which point he can cast a Forte Heavy Attack, switching his stances and dealing lots of damage if his Ultimate was cast prior. Without his Ultimate available, Jingran deals much lower damage from his Forte Heavies as he cannot generate any Fire of Life without it. This also means the Ultimate should be used before any Forte Heavies for the Fire of Life buff to actually affect the Forte Heavies in question.

His Intro is also important to gain a massive amount of Fusion DMG Bonus, and only casting a maximum of 4 Forte Heavies is intended, as he cannot generate any more Forte from his Forte Heavies after the 3rd cast (so you can get up to 4 casts total including the initial build-up from Intro and Ultimate).

Lastly, his Skills don't share cooldowns in between stances, so that means he gains access to 1 Skill chain per Yin and Yang stance per rotation. As a lot of his damage is gated behind his Intro and Ultimate and he can only cast a maximum of 4 Forte Heavies without his rotation becoming extremely slow, his quickswap potential is quite restricted, and a quickswap rotation loop that generates even one extra Forte Heavy per rotation won't happen in his best team without being too slow to be worth it.

So overall, his rotation is forced into using his Ultimate right after his Intro, at which point one Forte Heavy may be cast, then per Forte Heavy: a Basic chain, and 2 chains of Skills, 1 per stance, without much room for doing anything extra beyond some extra Basic Attacks, provided you have some rotation time to spare.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: Jingran is a very strong meta contender on his release, even though his ceiling doesn't get much higher than his baseline performance. That baseline performance is so strong and accessible, that Jingran possesses a good variety of strong teams, and a lot of inherent value to your account. Even if Jingran is one of the most Signature weapon-reliant characters in the game, as a Heavy Attack damage dealer he can easily go into F2P teams like Rebecca/Mortefi+Verina, by using a clever workaround to his Shield teammate restriction. Indeed, it's possible to use Main Echoes that generate Shields on his Supports for him to generate his Ghost Shroud nearly as efficiently as he would with Iuno on the team, providing nearly as much Fusion DMG Bonus as in his ideal team, though not quite matching its power.

Indeed, Jingran is best used alongside Iuno and Shorekeeper, but that should make most realize he has a lot of success to be found in running general Heavy Attack-buffing Hybrids and general Supports. Being second best used in a Mono Fusion setup with Mortefi and Lupa, he can also find success by just running Rebecca or Mortefi alongside Shorekeeper or Verina, those teams being largely on par with the Cartethyia to Galbrena generation of DPS characters, thanks to the Shield teammate bypass trick we mentioned earlier, as well as the fact that Jingran isn't HP-scaling like Cartethyia, but rather HP-converting, like Brant is with Energy Regen. Possessing good AoE and a top tier modern damage ceiling, Jingran is undeniably a very strong all-rounder DPS.

In conclusion, Jingran is a top tier Fusion Heavy Attack DPS who works amazingly well if you want to consider getting him alongside his Signature weapon. Past this point, he'll deliver satisfactory performance to be up to clearing some of the easier endgames effortlessly, with plenty of room for teammate upgrades to easily handle the hardest content the game currently has to offer, all the while the more optimizing players will find enjoyment in clearing hard content with him on budget teams, making him a versatile and strong DPS character at once.

synergies.commentary: Jingran's best 2 team archetypes are with the one buffer built towards Heavy Attack damage dealers that use shields and Mono Fusion. Iuno is the former and Lupa enables the latter, making them Jingran's 2 best synergies at the moment, though using them on the same team isn't recommended as Lupa wants to use a full team of Fusion characters.

Lupa's best partner in a Jingran team is Mortefi. He's a Fusion buffer for Heavy Attack damage dealers, so he enables Lupa while buffing Jingran by default. He can do so without Lupa on the team in a pinch, however Rebecca is generally a stronger Heavy Attack buffer if available (she just can't enable Lupa due to her being of the Electro element, so in Mono Fusion teams she will necessarily be worse).

Jingran scales with any general Support since there's no Support that's dedicated towards HP scalers or the Shield archetype. Generally, Shorekeeper is the most flexible and almost always the best idea. However, Mornye can be considered as a generally safe Support choice to enable Mono Fusion teams with Lupa. Verina is the permanently accessible Support option of choice if a replacement to Shorekeeper is needed.
